analysis:
Reviewed the changes in ProviderLoop+ModelLoading.swift, ProviderLoop+ModelSwitch.swift and ProviderLoop+PrefetchPublication.swift. The PR is lifecycle bookkeeping inside the provider process. It adds transitionGenerations.begin(.modelLoading) and begin(.modelLoading, subject:) in the load path, begin(.modelSwitch) in switchModels (ModelSwitch.swift:46), and beginModelAdvertisementOccurrence(modelId) in PrefetchPublication.swift:48. It also adds reconcileAutopilotPlacements() in unloadModel (ModelLoading.swift:1148-1150), which runs after modelSlots.removeValue and before the later awaits. The patch excerpt shows autopilotAllowsModel renamed to autopilotServesModel at load-time model selection, and the evictableModelSlots comment/body text changed. The head text shows evictableModelSlots still excludes pinned, held, in-flight, reserved, unloading and MTP-retained slots, and unloadModel(forEviction:) still rechecks these conditions. The model-switch ownership and drain logic is unchanged apart from the begin call.

No change touches the coordinator wire contract, encryption, attestation, App Attest authorization, prefix-cache storage or fan helper. The relevant threats (T-041, TB-007 and the T-053 stale-authorization boundary) are not weakened by anything visible.

The definitions of transitionGenerations, beginModelAdvertisementOccurrence, reconcileAutopilotPlacements and autopilotServesModel are outside the supplied evidence. Two things are unverified. First, whether begin() is paired with a matching end/complete on every exit path, including the throw and cancel paths in the load flow, switchModels and prefetch publication. A missing pairing would be an availability hazard, but it cannot be confirmed from the diff. Second, whether autopilotServesModel preserves the authorization semantics of the old autopilotAllowsModel. Neither is evidence of a regression, and I report no findings.
